title.zh: 卷245 列傳三十二 刚林 冯铨 陈铭夏 陈之遴 刘正宗
title.en: Volume 245 Biographies 32: Gang Lin, Feng Quan, Chen Mingxia, Chen Zhilin, Liu Zhengzong
title.raw: 卷245 列傳三十二 刚林 冯铨 陈铭夏 陈之遴 刘正宗

sentences.zh: 剛林，瓜爾佳氏，字公茂，滿洲正黃旗人，世居蘇完。

translations.literal: Ganglin, of the Guwalgiya clan, styled Gongmao, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner whose family had long resided in Suwan.
translations.idiomatic: Ganglin, of the Guwalgiya clan, styled Gongmao, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner from a family that had long lived in Suwan.

sentences.zh: 初來歸，隸正藍旗，屬郡王阿達禮。

translations.literal: When he first came to submit, he was enrolled in the Plain Blue Banner and placed under Prince of the Second Rank Adali.
translations.idiomatic: When he first came over to submit, he was assigned to the Plain Blue Banner and placed under Prince Adali.

sentences.zh: 授筆帖式，掌繙譯漢文。

translations.literal: He was appointed a bithe clerk and put in charge of translating Chinese texts.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a bithe clerk and placed in charge of translating Chinese documents.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，以漢文應試，中式舉人，命直文館。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he entered the examination in Chinese, passed as a provincial graduate, and was ordered to serve in the Literary Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 he sat for the examination in Chinese, passed as a provincial graduate, and was ordered to serve in the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，授國史院大學士，與範文程、希福等參與政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute and, together with Fan Wencheng, Xifu, and others, participated in governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he was made Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute and, with Fan Wencheng, Xifu, and others, took part in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 疏請重定部院承政以下官各五等，又疏請定試士之法，皆報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the ranks of officials from chief administrators of ministries and offices downward be set at five grades each, and again memorialized to fix the method of examining scholars; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials asking that officials from ministry and office chiefs downward be graded in five ranks each, and again asking that the method of examining scholars be fixed; both requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 太宗四征不庭，疆宇日闢。

translations.literal: The Taizong four times campaigned against those who did not submit, and the realm daily expanded.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong campaigned four times against recalcitrant foes, and the empire steadily expanded.

sentences.zh: 剛林屢奉使軍前，宣布威德，咸稱上旨。

translations.literal: Ganglin repeatedly went on missions to the front, proclaiming majesty and virtue, and everywhere conveyed the emperor's will.
translations.idiomatic: Ganglin was repeatedly sent to the front to proclaim the throne's majesty and virtue, and everywhere he spoke in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 積功，授世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was granted the hereditary office of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was granted the hereditary rank of niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 八年，阿達禮有罪，改隸正黃旗。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Adali was guilty of an offense, and Ganglin was transferred to the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Adali was found guilty, and Ganglin was transferred to the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎，進世職二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: When the Shizu established the capital, he was promoted to second-rank jalan janggin in hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu established the capital, he was promoted to second-rank jalan janggin in hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 三年、四年，迭主會試。

translations.literal: In the third and fourth years he presided over the metropolitan examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third and fourth years he presided over the metropolitan examinations in turn.

sentences.zh: 考滿，進世職一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: When his term of assessment was complete, he was promoted to first-rank adaha hafan in hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When his performance review was complete, he was promoted to first-rank adaha hafan in hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 五年，復進三等阿思哈尼哈番，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was further promoted to third-rank ashan i hafan and given the title "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was further promoted to third-rank ashan i hafan and granted the title "Bakshi."

sentences.zh: 六年，充太宗實錄總裁，復主會試。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Taizong and again presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of the Taizong Veritable Records and again presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 疏請令六科錄諸臣章奏並批答，月送史館，備纂修國史，報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the Six Offices of Scrutiny record all ministers' memorials together with imperial replies and send them monthly to the Historiography Institute for use in compiling the national history; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that the Six Offices of Scrutiny copy all ministers' memorials together with imperial replies and send them monthly to the Historiography Institute for compiling the national history; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，以編撰明史闕天啟四年至七年實錄，請敕懸賞購求；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because the compilation of the History of the Ming lacked the veritable records for Tianqi years four through seven, he asked that an edict be issued offering rewards for their purchase;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, because the compilation of the History of the Ming lacked the veritable records for Tianqi 4 through 7, he asked that an edict be issued offering rewards for their purchase;

sentences.zh: 崇禎一朝事責無考，其有野史、外傳，並令訪送。

translations.literal: For events of the Chongzhen reign there was no one to answer for them; any unofficial histories and external accounts were also to be sought out and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: For the Chongzhen reign there was no one who could be held accountable; any unofficial histories and outside accounts were likewise to be sought out and submitted.

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the appropriate office.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the responsible office.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾袞薨，得罪。

translations.literal: When the Prince Regent Dorgon died, Ganglin was condemned for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince Regent Dorgon died, Ganglin was condemned for his offenses.

sentences.zh: 剛林阿附睿親王，參與移永平密謀，又與大學士祁充格擅改太祖實錄，為睿親王削匿罪愆、增載功績，坐斬，籍沒。

translations.literal: Ganglin had fawned on the Prince Regent, participated in the secret plot to move to Yongping, and together with Grand Secretary Qi Chongge arbitrarily altered the Veritable Records of the Taizu to conceal the prince regent's guilt and add merit; he was sentenced to decapitation and his property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Ganglin had curried favor with the Prince Regent, took part in the secret plot to move the court to Yongping, and together with Grand Secretary Qi Chongge had arbitrarily altered the Taizu Veritable Records to conceal the prince regent's crimes and inflate his achievements; he was sentenced to decapitation and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 祁充格，烏蘇氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，世居瓦爾喀。

translations.literal: Qi Chongge, of the Wusu clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner whose family had long resided in Warka.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Chongge, of the Wusu clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner from a family long settled in Warka.

sentences.zh: 國初從其族吉思哈等來歸。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty he came to submit with his clansmen Jisiha and others.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he came over with his clansmen Jisiha and others.

sentences.zh: 太宗時號「四貝勒」，以祁充格嫺習文史，令掌書記。

translations.literal: In the time when the Taizong was styled the "Fourth Beile," because Qi Chongge was skilled in letters and history, he was ordered to manage secretarial work.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizong was still styled the "Fourth Beile," because Qi Chongge was well versed in letters and history, he was put in charge of secretarial work.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，初設六部，授禮部啟心郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong, when the Six Ministries were first established, he was appointed qixinlang of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 5, when the Six Ministries were first established, he was appointed qixinlang of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，考績，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, upon evaluation of performance, he was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after a performance review, he was appointed niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，睿親王多爾袞伐明，攻錦州，命鞏阿岱往濟師，祁充格從師有功，還報捷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, when the Prince Regent Dorgon attacked the Ming and besieged Jinzhou, he ordered Gongadai to go reinforce the army; Qi Chongge followed the army and had merit, and on returning reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1, when the Prince Regent Dorgon attacked the Ming and besieged Jinzhou, he sent Gongadai to reinforce the army; Qi Chongge followed the campaign with merit and returned to report victory.

sentences.zh: 三年，睿親王復伐明，太宗親餞於郊。

translations.literal: In the third year the Prince Regent again attacked the Ming, and the Taizong personally saw him off in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Prince Regent again attacked the Ming, and the Taizong personally saw him off outside the city.

sentences.zh: 祁充格以不啟豫親王多鐸從上出送，又於是日私往屯莊，坐死，命寬之，奪官，貫耳鞭責，以隸睿親王。

translations.literal: Qi Chongge, for not advising Prince Yu Dodo to accompany the emperor in escorting him and on that same day privately going to his estate, was liable to death; the order was to show leniency—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was whipped, and was placed under the Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Chongge, for failing to advise Prince Yu Dodo to join the emperor in escorting the army and for privately visiting his estate that same day, was liable to death; the sentence was commuted—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was flogged, and was placed under the Prince Regent.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，授弘文院大學士，充明史總裁官、冊封朝鮮世子正使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute, served as chief compiler of the History of the Ming, and was chief envoy enfeoffing the Korean heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute, made chief compiler of the History of the Ming, and sent as chief envoy to invest the Korean heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 四年，考滿，加授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when his assessment term was complete, he was additionally granted niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when his term review was complete, he was additionally granted niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 六年，充太宗實錄總裁官，與剛林等同主會試。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Taizong and jointly presided over the metropolitan examination with Ganglin and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of the Taizong Veritable Records and jointly presided over the metropolitan examination with Ganglin and others.

sentences.zh: 八年，與剛林同誅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was executed together with Ganglin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was executed together with Ganglin.

sentences.zh: 馮銓，字振鷺，順天涿州人。

translations.literal: Feng Quan, styled Zhenlu, was a native of Zhuozhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan, styled Zhenlu, was a native of Zhuozhou in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Wanli reign of the Ming, he was appointed reviewing secretary.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Ming Wanli reign, he was appointed reviewing secretary.

sentences.zh: 諂事魏忠賢，累遷文淵閣大學士兼戶部尚書，加少保兼太子太保，以微忤罷去。

translations.literal: He flattered and served Wei Zhongxian, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall concurrently Minister of Revenue, and given the added titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; for a minor offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He fawned on Wei Zhongxian and rose in succession to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall and concurrent Minister of Revenue, with the added titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; he was dismissed after a minor offense.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝既誅忠賢，得銓罷官後壽忠賢百韻詩，論杖徒，贖為民。

translations.literal: After the Chongzhen Emperor had executed Zhongxian, Quan's hundred-rhyme birthday poem for Zhongxian written after his dismissal was discovered; he was sentenced to beating and penal servitude, and after ransom was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chongzhen Emperor executed Zhongxian, a hundred-rhyme birthday poem Quan had written for Zhongxian after his dismissal came to light; he was sentenced to beating and penal servitude, then ransomed back to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，睿親王既定京師，以書徵銓，銓聞命即至，賚冠服、鞍馬、銀幣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, after the Prince Regent had secured the capital, he summoned Feng Quan by letter; Quan came as soon as he received the order and was rewarded with court dress, saddle horses, and silver coins.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, after the Prince Regent had secured the capital, he summoned Feng Quan by letter; Quan came at once and was rewarded with court dress, saddle horses, and silver.

sentences.zh: 令以大學士原銜入內院佐理機務，與大學士洪承疇疏請復明票擬舊制，又與大學士謝升等議定郊社、宗廟樂章。

translations.literal: He was ordered to enter the Inner Court to assist in state affairs with his former grand secretary title, and together with Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou memorialized to restore the Ming practice of memorial drafting with approval slips; together with Grand Secretary Xie Sheng and others he also settled the ceremonial music for suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to enter the Inner Court to assist in state affairs under his former grand secretary title; with Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou he memorialized to restore the Ming practice of drafting memorials with approval slips, and with Grand Secretary Xie Sheng and others he also settled the ceremonial music for suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，世祖禦皇極門受賀，給事中孫承澤疏糾朝班雜亂，語侵內院。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month the Shizu received congratulations at the Huangji Gate; supervising secretary Sun Chengze memorialized criticizing the disorder in the court ranks, with language impugning the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month the Shizu received congratulations at the Huangji Gate; supervising secretary Sun Chengze memorialized against the disorder in the court ranks, with language that impugned the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 銓與升、承疇乞罷，諭令益殫忠猷，以襄新治。

translations.literal: Quan together with Sheng and Chengchou begged to resign; an edict ordered them instead to devote themselves more fully in loyalty and assist the new governance.
translations.idiomatic: Quan, together with Sheng and Chengchou, asked to resign; an edict ordered them instead to devote themselves more fully and assist the new regime.

sentences.zh: 二年，授弘文院大學士兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute concurrently Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute and concurrent Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 御史吳達劾銓向降將薑瓖索銀三萬，許以封拜，未稱其意；

translations.literal: Censor Wu Da memorialized that Quan had demanded thirty thousand taels of silver from the surrendered general Jiang Xiang, promising him enfeoffment, which did not satisfy Jiang;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Da memorialized that Quan had demanded thirty thousand taels of silver from the surrendered general Jiang Xiang, promising him enfeoffment, which did not satisfy Jiang;

sentences.zh: 內院政本所關，乃令其子源淮擅入，張宴歡飲。

translations.literal: Since the Inner Court concerned the foundation of government, he nevertheless allowed his son Yuanhuai to enter without authorization, hold banquets and drink in revelry.
translations.idiomatic: Even though the Inner Court touched the very foundation of government, he nevertheless allowed his son Yuanhuai to enter without authorization and hold banquets there in revelry.

sentences.zh: 給事中許作梅、莊憲祖、杜立德，御史王守履、羅國士、鄧孕槐、桑芸等亦交章劾銓得招撫侍郎江禹緒金；

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Xu Zuomei, Zhuang Xianzu, and Du Lide, and censors Wang Shoulü, Luo Guoshi, Deng Yuhuai, and Sang Yun also jointly memorialized that Quan received gold from Pacification Vice Minister Jiang Yuxu;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Xu Zuomei, Zhuang Xianzu, and Du Lide, and censors Wang Shoulü, Luo Guoshi, Deng Yuhuai, and Sang Yun also submitted joint memorials accusing Quan of receiving gold from Pacification Vice Minister Jiang Yuxu;

sentences.zh: 為源淮賄招撫侍郎孫之獬充標下中軍；

translations.literal: that for Yuanhuai he bribed Pacification Vice Minister Sun Zhixie to appoint him as a middle army officer under his command;
translations.idiomatic: that he bribed Pacification Vice Minister Sun Zhixie to appoint Yuanhuai as a middle army officer under his command;

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李若琳為銓黨羽，庸懦無行。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Li Ruolin was Quan's partisan, timid and weak in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Li Ruolin was Quan's partisan, timid and without proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 御史李森先疏繼入，語尤峻，略謂：「明二百餘年國祚，壞於忠賢，而忠賢當日殺戮賢良，通賄謀逆，皆成於銓。

translations.literal: Censor Li Senxian submitted a follow-up memorial with especially harsh language, in part stating: "The Ming dynasty's more than two hundred years of fortune was ruined by Zhongxian, and when Zhongxian slaughtered the worthy, took bribes, and plotted rebellion, it was all brought about by Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Senxian followed with a memorial in especially harsh language, stating in part: "The Ming dynasty's more than two hundred years of fortune was ruined by Zhongxian, and when Zhongxian slaughtered the worthy, took bribes, and plotted rebellion, it was all brought about by Quan.

sentences.zh: 此通國共知者。

translations.literal: This is known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 請立彰大法，戮之於市。」

translations.literal: I ask that the great law be publicly upheld and that he be executed in the marketplace."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the law be upheld in full public view and that he be executed in the marketplace."

sentences.zh: 疏並下刑部鞫問，刑部以所劾不實，啟睿親王。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down together to the Ministry of Justice for interrogation; the Ministry of Justice reported that the accusations were not substantiated and submitted this to the Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Justice for interrogation; the ministry reported that the accusations were not substantiated and submitted this to the Prince Regent.

sentences.zh: 王集廷臣覆讞，以銓降後與之獬、若琳皆先薙發，之獬家男婦並改滿裝，諸臣遂謀陷害。

translations.literal: The prince assembled court ministers to review the case and found that after Quan surrendered, he, Zhixie, and Ruolin had all shaved their heads first; the men and women of Zhixie's household all changed to Manchu dress, and the ministers therefore plotted to frame them.
translations.idiomatic: The prince assembled court ministers to review the case and found that after Quan surrendered, he, Zhixie, and Ruolin had all shaved their heads first; the men and women of Zhixie's household had all adopted Manchu dress, and the ministers therefore plotted to frame them.

sentences.zh: 王謂三人者皆恪遵本朝法度，詰責科道諸臣。

translations.literal: The prince said all three strictly followed the laws of the dynasty and rebuked the supervising secretaries and censors.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said all three had strictly followed the laws of the dynasty and rebuked the supervising secretaries and censors.

sentences.zh: 給事中龔鼎孳言銓附忠賢作惡，銓亦反詰鼎孳嘗降李自成。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Gong Dingzi said Quan had attached himself to Zhongxian to do evil; Quan in turn accused Dingzi of once having surrendered to Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Gong Dingzi said Quan had attached himself to Zhongxian to do evil; Quan in turn accused Dingzi of once having surrendered to Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 王問鼎孳：「銓語實否？」

translations.literal: The prince asked Dingzi: "Is Quan's statement true?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked Dingzi: "Is what Quan says true?"

sentences.zh: 鼎孳曰：「豈惟鼎孳，魏徵亦嘗降唐太宗。」

translations.literal: Dingzi said: "Not only Dingzi—Wei Zheng also once surrendered to Tang Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi said: "Not only I—Wei Zheng also once surrendered to Tang Taizong."

sentences.zh: 王因斥鼎孳，遂寢其事。

translations.literal: The prince thereupon rebuked Dingzi and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The prince thereupon rebuked Dingzi, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 以森先言過甚，奪官，互見森先傳。

translations.literal: Because Senxian's words were excessive, his office was stripped; see also the biography of Senxian.
translations.idiomatic: Because Senxian's language was excessive, his office was stripped; see also the biography of Senxian.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，銓疏言：「臣蒙特召入內院，列同官舊臣之前，臣固辭不敢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Quan memorialized, stating: "I received the special summons to enter the Inner Court, placed ahead of old ministers among my colleagues—I firmly declined and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Quan memorialized, stating: "I received a special summons to enter the Inner Court and was placed ahead of the older ministers among my colleagues; I firmly declined and did not dare accept.

sentences.zh: 攝政王面諭：'國家尊賢敬客，卿其勿讓！

translations.literal: The Prince Regent instructed him face to face: "The state respects the worthy and treats guests with honor—do not decline!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent told him in person: "The state honors the worthy and treats guests with respect—do not decline!"

sentences.zh: '今海宇漸平，制度略定。

translations.literal: Now the realm is gradually pacified and institutions are largely established.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is gradually pacified and institutions are largely in place.

sentences.zh: 金台駿骨，暫示招徠。

translations.literal: The golden platform and fine steed are a temporary gesture of recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: The golden platform and fine steed were a temporary gesture of recruitment.

sentences.zh: 久假不歸，實逾涯分。

translations.literal: To borrow honor long without yielding truly oversteps one's bounds.
translations.idiomatic: To hold borrowed honor so long without yielding truly oversteps what is due me.

sentences.zh: 況叨承寵命，賜婚滿洲，理當附籍滿洲編氓之末。

translations.literal: Moreover, having received gracious appointments and been given a Manchu marriage, by rights I should be enrolled at the end of the Manchu register.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, having received gracious appointments and been given a Manchu marriage, by rights I ought to be enrolled at the end of the Manchu register.

sentences.zh: 回繹尊賢敬客之諭，輾轉悚懼，特懇改列範文程、剛林後。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the instruction to respect the worthy and treat guests with honor, I am repeatedly fearful and trembling, and earnestly beg to be moved to after Fan Wencheng and Ganglin.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the instruction to honor the worthy and treat guests with respect, I am repeatedly fearful and earnestly beg to be moved to after Fan Wencheng and Ganglin.

sentences.zh: 如以新舊為次，並當列祁充格、寧完我後。」

translations.literal: If precedence is by old and new, I should in any case be placed after Qi Chongge and Ning Wanwo."
translations.idiomatic: If precedence is by seniority, I should in any case be placed after Qi Chongge and Ning Wanwo."

sentences.zh: 得旨：「天下一統，滿、漢無分別。

translations.literal: Receiving the rescript: "Under unified rule throughout the realm, Manchu and Han are not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He received the rescript: "Under unified rule throughout the realm, Manchu and Han are not to be distinguished.

sentences.zh: 內院職掌等級，原有成規，不必再定。」

translations.literal: The duties and ranks of the Inner Court already have established rules and need not be set anew."
translations.idiomatic: The duties and ranks of the Inner Court already have established rules and need not be fixed again."

sentences.zh: 是年命典會試，列範文程、剛林後，寧完我前。

translations.literal: That year he was ordered to preside over the metropolitan examination, ranked after Fan Wencheng and Ganglin but before Ning Wanwo.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was ordered to preside over the metropolitan examination, ranked after Fan Wencheng and Ganglin but before Ning Wanwo.

sentences.zh: 四年，复典會試。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 六年，加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the added titles of Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given the added titles of Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八年，上親覈諸大臣功績，諭：「銓先經吳達奏劾得叛將薑瓖賄，便當引去；

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor personally verified the achievements of the great ministers and instructed: "When Quan was earlier memorialized against by Wu Da for receiving bribes from the rebellious general Jiang Xiang, he ought to have withdrawn;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor personally reviewed the achievements of the great ministers and instructed: "When Quan was earlier memorialized against by Wu Da for taking bribes from the rebellious general Jiang Xiang, he ought to have withdrawn;

sentences.zh: 乃隱忍居官，七年以來，無所建白：令致仕。

translations.literal: yet he concealedly remained in office, and in seven years has offered nothing constructive: order him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: yet he quietly remained in office and in seven years has offered nothing constructive: order him to retire.

sentences.zh: 李若琳憸險專擅，與銓朋比為奸，奪官，永不敘用。」

translations.literal: Li Ruolin is crafty, dangerous, and monopolizes power; together with Quan he forms a faction to do evil—strip his office and never employ him again."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruolin is crafty, dangerous, and monopolizes power; together with Quan he forms a faction to do evil—strip his office and never employ him again."

sentences.zh: 銓既罷，代以陳名夏，坐事奪官；

translations.literal: After Quan was dismissed, Chen Mingxia replaced him but was stripped of office for an offense;
translations.idiomatic: After Quan was dismissed, Chen Mingxia replaced him but was stripped of office for an offense;

sentences.zh: 代以陳之遴，亦不久罷。

translations.literal: Chen Zhilin replaced him but was also soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilin replaced him but was also soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上復召銓還，諭曰：「國家用人，使功不如使過。

translations.literal: The emperor again recalled Quan and instructed: "In employing men the state finds it better to use those who have erred than those who have merely succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Quan and instructed: "In employing men, the state finds it better to use those who have erred than those who have merely succeeded.

sentences.zh: 銓素有才學，博洽諳練，朕特召用，以觀自新。」

translations.literal: Quan has long had talent and learning, is broadly versed and experienced—I specially recall him to see whether he will reform."
translations.idiomatic: Quan has long had talent and learning and is broadly versed and experienced; I specially recall him to see whether he will reform."

sentences.zh: 銓至，召見，又與承疇、文程等同夕對論翰林官賢否，上曰：「朕將親試之！」

translations.literal: When Quan arrived and was granted audience, the emperor again discussed that evening with Chengchou, Wencheng, and others whether Hanlin officials were worthy or not, and said: "I shall personally examine them!"
translations.idiomatic: When Quan arrived and was granted audience, the emperor that evening discussed with Chengchou, Wencheng, and others whether the Hanlin officials were worthy, and said: "I shall examine them myself!"

sentences.zh: 銓奏曰：「南人優於文而行不符，北人短於文而行或善。

translations.literal: Quan memorialized: "Southerners are superior in letters but their conduct does not match; northerners are deficient in letters but their conduct may be good.
translations.idiomatic: Quan replied: "Southerners are superior in letters but their conduct does not match; northerners are weaker in letters but their conduct may be good.

sentences.zh: 今取文行兼優者用之可也。」

translations.literal: Now take those who excel in both letters and conduct and employ them."
translations.idiomatic: Take those who excel in both letters and conduct and employ them."

sentences.zh: 上頷之，仍授弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded in agreement and again appointed him Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in agreement and again appointed him Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 以議總兵任珍罪坐欺飾論絞，上命寬之。

translations.literal: For discussing the punishment of Regional Commander Ren Zhen and being convicted of deceitful concealment with a sentence of strangulation, the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: For discussing the punishment of Regional Commander Ren Zhen and being convicted of deceitful concealment with a sentence of strangulation, the emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 銓入謝，奏對失旨，諭誡之。

translations.literal: Quan entered to give thanks; his replies missed the imperial intent and he was admonished by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Quan entered to give thanks; his replies missed the imperial intent and he was admonished by edict.

sentences.zh: 龔鼎孳為左都御史，复劾銓，上命指實。

translations.literal: Gong Dingzi, as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, again memorialized against Quan; the emperor ordered specific facts.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Dingzi, as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, again memorialized against Quan; the emperor ordered him to cite specific facts.

sentences.zh: 鼎孳言銓罪過頗多，惟以密勿票擬，非如諸曹有實可指，上切責鼎孳。

translations.literal: Dingzi said Quan's offenses were many, but because he handled confidential memorial drafting with approval slips, unlike other offices there were no concrete facts to cite; the emperor sharply rebuked Dingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi said Quan's offenses were many, but because he handled confidential memorial drafting with approval slips, unlike other offices there were no concrete facts to cite; the emperor sharply rebuked Dingzi.

sentences.zh: 十二年，居母喪，命入直如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, while in mourning for his mother, he was ordered to enter duty as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, while in mourning for his mother, he was ordered to continue entering duty as before.

sentences.zh: 尋加少師兼太子太師。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上以銓衰老，加太保致仕，仍令在左右備顧問，銓疏請回籍，許之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, because the emperor considered Quan aged, he was given the added title of Grand Guardian and ordered to retire, yet still to remain nearby as consultant; Quan memorialized asking to return to his native place and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, because the emperor considered Quan aged, he was given the added title of Grand Guardian and ordered to retire, yet still to remain nearby as a consultant; Quan memorialized asking to return to his native place and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改設內閣，命以原銜兼中和殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Cabinet was newly established and he was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Zhonghe Hall with his former title.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the Cabinet was newly established, and he was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Zhonghe Hall under his former title.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，卒，諡文敏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi he died and was given the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 he died and was given the posthumous title Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 旋命削諡。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered stripped of the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered stripped of the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 孫之獬，山東淄川人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhixie was a native of Zichuan in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhixie was a native of Zichuan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明天啟進士，授檢討，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Tianqi reign of the Ming, he was appointed reviewing secretary and promoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Ming Tianqi reign, he was appointed reviewing secretary and promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 以爭毀三朝要典入逆案，削籍。

translations.literal: For striving to destroy the Essentials of Three Reigns and being entered in the case of the rebels, he was struck from the register.
translations.idiomatic: For striving to destroy the Essentials of Three Reigns and being entered in the case of the rebels, he was struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，侍郎王鰲永招撫山東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi Vice Minister Wang Aoyong pacified Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 Vice Minister Wang Aoyong pacified Shandong.

sentences.zh: 土寇攻淄川，之獬斥家財守城。

translations.literal: Local bandits attacked Zichuan; Zhixie spent his family wealth to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits attacked Zichuan; Zhixie spent his family wealth to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫方大猷上其事，召詣京師，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shandong Governor Fang Dayou reported the matter upward; he was summoned to the capital and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Governor Fang Dayou reported the matter upward; he was summoned to the capital and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二年，師克九江，之獬奏請往任招撫，從之，加兵部尚書銜以行。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the army captured Jiujiang, Zhixie memorialized asking to go and take up pacification duties; the request was granted, and he was given the provisional title of Minister of War for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the army captured Jiujiang, Zhixie memorialized asking to go and take up pacification duties; the request was granted, and he was given the provisional title of Minister of War for the journey.

sentences.zh: 三年，召還。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 總兵金聲桓劾之獬擅加副將高進庫、劉一鵬總兵銜，市恩構釁；

translations.literal: Regional Commander Jin Shenghuan memorialized that Zhixie had on his own authority given the provisional title of regional commander to Vice Commanders Gao Jinku and Liu Yipeng, currying favor and provoking conflict;
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Jin Shenghuan memorialized that Zhixie had on his own authority given the provisional title of regional commander to Vice Commanders Gao Jinku and Liu Yipeng, currying favor and provoking conflict;

sentences.zh: 之獬議撫諸將懷觀望，不力攻贛州。

translations.literal: Zhixie argued that the pacified generals were waiting to see which way things would go and did not press the attack on Ganzhou with full force.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixie argued that the pacified generals were holding back in watchful hesitation and did not press the attack on Ganzhou with full force.

sentences.zh: 之獬疏辨，下兵部議，奪之獬官。

translations.literal: Zhixie memorialized in his defense; the matter was sent down to the Ministry of War for deliberation, and Zhixie was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixie memorialized in his defense; the matter was referred to the Ministry of War for deliberation, and Zhixie was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 四年，土寇復攻淄川，之獬佐城守，城破，死之，諸孫從死者七人，下吏部議卹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year local bandits again attacked Zichuan; Zhixie assisted in defending the city; when the city fell he died in the fighting, and seven of his grandsons died with him; the matter was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel to deliberate on posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year local bandits again attacked Zichuan; Zhixie helped defend the city; when the city fell he died in the fighting, and seven of his grandsons died with him; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Personnel to decide on posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 侍郎陳名夏、金之俊議復之獬官，予卹；

translations.literal: Vice Ministers Chen Mingxia and Jin Zhijun argued that Zhixie's office should be restored and posthumous honors granted;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers Chen Mingxia and Jin Zhijun argued that Zhixie's office should be restored and posthumous honors granted;

sentences.zh: 馬光輝及啟心郎寧古里議之獬已削籍，不當予卹。

translations.literal: Ma Guanghui and qixinlang Ningguli argued that Zhixie had already been struck from the register and ought not to receive posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guanghui and qixinlang Ningguli argued that Zhixie had already been struck from the register and ought not to receive posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 兩議上，命用光輝議。

translations.literal: Both opinions were submitted upward, and the order was to follow Guanghui's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Both opinions were submitted upward, and the order was to follow Guanghui's opinion.

sentences.zh: 李若琳，山東新城人。

translations.literal: Li Ruolin was a native of Xincheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruolin was a native of Xincheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明天啟進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Tianqi reign of the Ming, he was appointed reviewing secretary.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Ming Tianqi reign, he was appointed reviewing secretary.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，起原官，累遷少詹事，兼國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was restored to his former office and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he was restored to his former office and rose in succession to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 詹事府裁，改翰林院侍讀學士，兼祭酒如故。

translations.literal: When the Household of the Heir Apparent was abolished, he was changed to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, still concurrently Chancellor as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Household of the Heir Apparent was abolished, he was made Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy while still serving concurrently as Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 二年，請更定孔子神牌，復元制曰大成至聖文宣王，下禮部議，定稱大成至聖先師。

translations.literal: In the second year he asked that Confucius's spirit tablet be revised, restoring the Yuan designation as "Perfect Sage and Exalted King of Culture and Propagation"; the matter was sent down to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation, which fixed the title as "Perfect Sage and Exalted Teacher."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he asked that Confucius's spirit tablet be revised, restoring the Yuan designation as Perfect Sage and Exalted King of Culture and Propagation; the Ministry of Rites deliberated and fixed the title as Perfect Sage and Exalted Teacher.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，進尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Minister.

sentences.zh: 六年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 既罷歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: After he was dismissed and returned home, he died before long.
translations.idiomatic: After he was dismissed and returned home, he died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 陳名夏，字百史，江南溧陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia, styled Baishi, was a native of Liyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia, styled Baishi, was a native of Liyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官修撰，兼戶、兵二科都給事中。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he served as compiler and concurrently held the posts of supervising secretary for both the Revenue and War sections.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Ming Chongzhen reign, he served as compiler and concurrently held the posts of supervising secretary for both the Revenue and War sections.

sentences.zh: 降李自成。

translations.literal: He surrendered to Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered to Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 福王時，入從賊案。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he was entered in the case of those who followed the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was entered in the case of those who followed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，詣大名降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he went to Daming to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he went to Daming to surrender.

sentences.zh: 以保定巡撫王文奎薦，復原官。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Baoding Governor Wang Wenkui, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Baoding Governor Wang Wenkui, he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 入謁睿親王，請正大位。

translations.literal: On entering audience with the Prince Regent, he asked that the throne be formally taken.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience with the Prince Regent, he asked that the throne be formally assumed.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「本朝自有家法，非爾所知也。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "Our dynasty has its own house laws—this is not for you to know."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "Our dynasty has its own house laws—this is not for you to know."

sentences.zh: 旋超擢吏部侍郎，兼翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted above the usual rank to Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrently Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted above the usual rank to Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 師定江南，九卿科道議南京設官。

translations.literal: When the army secured Jiangnan, the Nine Ministers and the supervising secretaries and censors deliberated on establishing offices at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the army secured Jiangnan, the Nine Ministers and the supervising secretaries and censors deliberated on establishing offices at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 名夏言：「國家定鼎神京，居北制南。

translations.literal: Mingxia said: "The state has established the capital at the divine capital and governs the south from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia said: "The state has established the capital at the divine capital and governs the south from the north.

sentences.zh: 不當如前朝稱都會，設官如諸行省。」

translations.literal: It should not, as in the previous dynasty, be styled a capital metropolis, with offices set up like those of the various provinces."
translations.idiomatic: It should not, as under the previous dynasty, be styled a capital metropolis with offices set up like those of the provinces."

sentences.zh: 疏入稱旨。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it met with imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted it met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 三年，居父喪，命奪情任事，請終制，賜白金五百，暫假歸葬，仍給俸贍其孥在京者。

translations.literal: In the third year, while in mourning for his father, he was ordered to set aside mourning and continue in office; he asked to complete the mourning period and was granted five hundred taels of white silver, given temporary leave to return home for the burial, and still provided salary to support his family remaining in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while in mourning for his father, he was ordered to set aside mourning and continue in office; he asked to complete the mourning period and was granted five hundred taels of silver, given temporary leave to return home for the burial, and still provided salary to support his family in the capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，初設六部漢尚書，授名夏吏部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Han Chinese ministers were first appointed to the Six Ministries, Mingxia was appointed Minister of Personnel and given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Han Chinese ministers were first appointed to the Six Ministries, Mingxia was made Minister of Personnel and given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八年，授弘文院大學士，進少保，兼太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute, promoted to Junior Guardian, and given the concurrent title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute, promoted to Junior Guardian, and given the concurrent title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 名夏任吏部時，滿尚書譚泰阿睿親王，擅權，名夏附之亂政。

translations.literal: When Mingxia served as Minister of Personnel, the Manchu Minister Tan Tai fawned on the Prince Regent, usurped power, and Mingxia attached himself to him and helped disorder government.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingxia served as Minister of Personnel, the Manchu Minister Tan Tai fawned on the Prince Regent, usurped power, and Mingxia attached himself to him and helped disorder government.

sentences.zh: 睿親王薨，是夏，御史張煊劾名夏結黨行私，銓選不公，下王大臣會鞫，譚泰袒名夏，坐煊誣奏，論死。

translations.literal: When the Prince Regent died, that summer Censor Zhang Xuan memorialized against Mingxia for forming factions and pursuing private ends and for unfair appointments; the matter was sent down to the prince and great ministers for joint interrogation; Tan Tai shielded Mingxia, and Xuan was convicted of false memorializing and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince Regent died, that summer Censor Zhang Xuan memorialized against Mingxia for forming factions, pursuing private ends, and making unfair appointments; the prince and great ministers were ordered to interrogate the case jointly; Tan Tai shielded Mingxia, and Xuan was convicted of false memorializing and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 語詳煊傳。

translations.literal: The details are given in the biography of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The details are given in the biography of Xuan.

sentences.zh: 是時御史盛復選亦以劾名夏坐黜。

translations.literal: At that time Censor Sheng Fuxuan was also dismissed for memorializing against Mingxia.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Censor Sheng Fuxuan was also dismissed for memorializing against Mingxia.

sentences.zh: 迨秋，譚泰以罪誅，九年春，復命王大臣按煊所劾名夏罪狀，名夏辨甚力。

translations.literal: By autumn Tan Tai was executed for crimes; in the spring of the ninth year the prince and great ministers were again ordered to investigate the offenses against Mingxia memorialized by Xuan, and Mingxia defended himself vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn Tan Tai was executed for crimes; in the spring of the ninth year the prince and great ministers were again ordered to investigate the offenses against Mingxia that Xuan had memorialized, and Mingxia defended himself vigorously.

sentences.zh: 及屢見詰難，詞窮，泣訴投誠有功，冀貸死。

translations.literal: When repeatedly pressed with hard questions, his words ran out; weeping, he pleaded that his surrender had been meritorious, hoping to be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When repeatedly pressed with hard questions, his words ran out; weeping, he pleaded that his surrender had been meritorious, hoping to be spared death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此輾轉矯詐之小人也，罪實難逭！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is a petty man who twists and turns in deceit—his guilt truly cannot be escaped!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is a petty man who twists and turns in deceit—his guilt truly cannot be escaped!

sentences.zh: 但朕已有旨，凡與譚泰事干連者，皆赦勿問。

translations.literal: But I have already issued an edict that all those connected with Tan Tai's affairs are to be pardoned and not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: But I have already issued an edict that all those connected with Tan Tai's affairs are to be pardoned and not investigated.

sentences.zh: 若復罪名夏，是為不信。」

translations.literal: If Mingxia were condemned again, that would make me untrustworthy."
translations.idiomatic: If Mingxia were condemned again, that would make me untrustworthy."

sentences.zh: 因宥之，命奪官，仍給俸，發正黃旗，與閒散官隨朝，諭令自新。

translations.literal: He was therefore pardoned, ordered stripped of office but still given salary, sent to the Plain Yellow Banner to attend court with idle officials, and instructed to reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore pardoned, stripped of office but still given salary, sent to the Plain Yellow Banner to attend court with idle officials, and instructed to reform himself.

sentences.zh: 十年，復授秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again appointed Grand Secretary of the Secretariat Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was again appointed Grand Secretary of the Secretariat Institute.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書員缺，侍郎孫承澤請以名夏兼攝，上責承澤以侍郎舉大學士，非體。

translations.literal: When the post of Minister of Personnel fell vacant, Vice Minister Sun Chengze asked that Mingxia concurrently act in the post; the emperor rebuked Chengze for a vice minister recommending a grand secretary, which was improper.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Minister of Personnel fell vacant, Vice Minister Sun Chengze asked that Mingxia concurrently act in the post; the emperor rebuked Chengze for a vice minister recommending a grand secretary, which was improper.

sentences.zh: 翌日，命名夏署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The next day Mingxia was ordered to act as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Mingxia was ordered to act as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上時幸內院，恆諭諸臣：「滿、漢一體，毋互結黨與。」

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Inner Court he constantly instructed the ministers: "Manchu and Han are one body—do not form factions among yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Inner Court he constantly instructed the ministers: "Manchu and Han are one body—do not form factions among yourselves."

sentences.zh: 名夏或強辭以對，上戒之曰：「爾勿怙過，自貽伊戚。」

translations.literal: Mingxia sometimes answered with forced arguments; the emperor warned him: "Do not rely on past offenses and bring calamity on yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia sometimes answered with forced arguments; the emperor warned him: "Do not rely on past offenses and bring calamity on yourself."

sentences.zh: 諸大臣議總兵任珍罪，皆以珍擅殺，其孥怨望，宜傅重比。

translations.literal: The great ministers deliberated on the offense of Regional Commander Ren Zhen and all held that Ren had killed without authorization, that his family resented and looked on with discontent, and that a heavy penalty should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers deliberated on the offense of Regional Commander Ren Zhen and all held that Ren had killed without authorization, that his family resented and looked on with discontent, and that a heavy penalty should be applied.

sentences.zh: 名夏與陳之遴、金之俊等異議，坐欺矇，論死，复寬之，但鐫秩俸，任事如故。

translations.literal: Mingxia, together with Chen Zhilin, Jin Zhijun, and others, held a different opinion; he was convicted of deceitful concealment and sentenced to death, but was again shown leniency—only his rank and salary were reduced, and he continued in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia, together with Chen Zhilin, Jin Zhijun, and others, held a different opinion; he was convicted of deceitful concealment and sentenced to death, but was again shown leniency—only his rank and salary were reduced, and he continued in office as before.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大學士寧完我劾之，略言：「名夏屢蒙赦宥，尚复包藏禍心。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Grand Secretary Ning Wanwo memorialized against him, stating in part: "Mingxia has repeatedly received pardons, yet still harbors treacherous intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Grand Secretary Ning Wanwo memorialized against him, stating in part: "Mingxia has repeatedly received pardons, yet still harbors treacherous intent.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂臣曰：'留發复衣冠，天下即太平。

translations.literal: He once told me: 'If hair is kept and Han dress restored, the realm will at once be at peace.'
translations.idiomatic: He once told me: "If hair is kept and Han dress restored, the realm will at once be at peace."

sentences.zh: '其情叵測。

translations.literal: His intent is hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: His intent is hard to fathom.

sentences.zh: 名夏子掖臣，居鄉暴惡，士民怨恨。

translations.literal: Mingxia's son Yechen, while living in the countryside, was violent and wicked, and scholars and common people resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia's son Yechen, while living in the countryside, was violent and wicked, and scholars and common people resented him.

sentences.zh: 移居江寧，佔入官園宅，關通納賄，名夏明知故縱。

translations.literal: After moving to Jiangning he seized government gardens and residences, used connections to take bribes, and Mingxia knowingly allowed it.
translations.idiomatic: After moving to Jiangning he seized government gardens and residences, used connections to take bribes, and Mingxia knowingly allowed it.

sentences.zh: 名夏署吏部尚書，破格擢其私交趙延先，給事中郭一鶚疏及之，名夏欲加罪，以劉正宗不平而止。

translations.literal: When Mingxia was acting Minister of Personnel he promoted his private associate Zhao Yanxian by breaking precedent; supervising secretary Guo Yihu memorialized against this, and Mingxia wanted to punish him but stopped because Liu Zhengzong objected.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingxia was acting Minister of Personnel he promoted his private associate Zhao Yanxian by breaking precedent; supervising secretary Guo Yihu memorialized against this, and Mingxia wanted to punish him but stopped because Liu Zhengzong objected.

sentences.zh: 浙江道員史儒綱為名夏姻家，坐事奪官逮問，名夏必欲為之复官。

translations.literal: Zhejiang circuit official Shi Rugang was Mingxia's in-law; when he was stripped of office and arrested for questioning over an offense, Mingxia insisted on restoring his office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang circuit official Shi Rugang was Mingxia's in-law; when he was stripped of office and arrested for questioning over an offense, Mingxia insisted on restoring his office.

sentences.zh: 給事中魏象樞與名夏姻家，有連坐事，應左遷，僅票俸。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wei Xiangshu was Mingxia's in-law; in a case of joint liability he should have been demoted but received only a salary reduction on the approval slip.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wei Xiangshu was Mingxia's in-law; in a case of joint liability he should have been demoted but received only a salary reduction on the approval slip.

sentences.zh: 護黨市恩，於此可見。

translations.literal: Protecting his faction and currying favor can be seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: His protection of faction and currying of favor can be seen in this.

sentences.zh: 臣等職掌票擬，一字輕重，關係公私；

translations.literal: We are charged with drafting approval slips; the weight of a single character concerns public and private interest;
translations.idiomatic: We are charged with drafting approval slips; the weight of a single character concerns public and private interest;

sentences.zh: 立簿注姓，以防推諉。

translations.literal: ledgers are kept recording names to prevent shifting blame.
translations.idiomatic: ledgers are kept recording names to prevent shifting blame.

sentences.zh: 名夏私自塗抹一百十四字。

translations.literal: Mingxia on his own authority altered one hundred and fourteen characters.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia on his own authority altered one hundred and fourteen characters.

sentences.zh: 上命誥誡科道官結黨，名夏擅加抹改，其欺罔類是。

translations.literal: The emperor had ordered an admonitory edict against supervising secretaries and censors forming factions; Mingxia had on his own authority added alterations—his deceit was of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered an admonitory edict against supervising secretaries and censors forming factions; Mingxia had on his own authority added alterations—his deceit was of the same kind.

sentences.zh: 請敕大臣鞫實，法斷施行。」

translations.literal: I ask that great ministers be ordered to investigate the facts and that the law be applied in judgment."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that great ministers be ordered to investigate the facts and that the law be applied in judgment."

sentences.zh: 疏下廷臣會鞫，名夏辨諸款皆虛，惟「留發复衣冠」，實有其語。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to court ministers for joint interrogation; Mingxia argued that all counts were false except "keeping hair and restoring Han dress," for which he had indeed spoken such words.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to court ministers for joint interrogation; Mingxia argued that all counts were false except "keeping hair and restoring Han dress," for which he had indeed spoken such words.

sentences.zh: 完我與正宗共證名夏諸罪狀皆實，讞成，論斬，上命改絞。

translations.literal: Wanwo and Zhengzong jointly testified that all of Mingxia's offenses were true; when the verdict was completed he was sentenced to decapitation, and the emperor ordered the sentence changed to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo and Zhengzong jointly testified that all of Mingxia's offenses were true; when the verdict was completed he was sentenced to decapitation, and the emperor ordered the sentence changed to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 掖臣逮治，杖戍。

translations.literal: Yechen was arrested and punished; he was beaten and sent to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Yechen was arrested and punished; he was beaten and sent to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 陳之遴，字彥升，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhilin, styled Yansheng, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilin, styled Yansheng, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，自編修遷中允。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he was promoted from compiler to junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Ming Chongzhen reign, he was promoted from compiler to junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，來降，授秘書院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he came to surrender and was appointed Reader-in-Waiting of the Secretariat Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he came to surrender and was appointed Reader-in-Waiting of the Secretariat Institute.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，加右都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the added title of Censor-in-Chief of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given the added title of Censor-in-Chief of the Right.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 御史張煊劾大學士陳名夏，語涉之遴，鞫不實，免議，加太子太保，九年，授弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Xuan memorialized against Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia with language implicating Zhilin; interrogation found no substance and he was exempted from censure; he was given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; in the ninth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Xuan memorialized against Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia with language implicating Zhilin; interrogation found no substance and he was exempted from censure; he was given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; in the ninth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 時捕治京師巨猾李應試，王大臣會鞫，之遴默不語，王大臣詰之，之遴曰：「上立置應試於法則已，如或免死，則必受其害，是以不言。」

translations.literal: At that time the great rogue of the capital Li Yingshi was being arrested and tried; the prince and great ministers jointly interrogated the case; Zhilin remained silent; when the prince and great ministers pressed him, Zhilin said: "If Your Majesty at once puts Yingshi to the law, that is enough; but if he is spared death, I will surely suffer harm from him—therefore I do not speak."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the great rogue of the capital Li Yingshi was being arrested and tried; the prince and great ministers jointly interrogated the case; Zhilin remained silent; when they pressed him, Zhilin said: "If Your Majesty at once puts Yingshi to the law, that is enough; but if he is spared death, I will surely suffer harm from him—therefore I do not speak."

sentences.zh: 王大臣等以聞，上以詰之遴，疏引罪。

translations.literal: The prince and great ministers reported this upward; the emperor questioned Zhilin, and he memorialized accepting guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The prince and great ministers reported this upward; the emperor questioned Zhilin, and he memorialized accepting guilt.

sentences.zh: 上以之遴既悔過，宥之。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered that Zhilin had already repented, he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor considered that Zhilin had already repented, he pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 議總兵任珍罪，與名夏及金之俊持異議，坐罪，寬貸如名夏。

translations.literal: In deliberating on the offense of Regional Commander Ren Zhen he held a different opinion together with Mingxia and Jin Zhijun; he was convicted but shown leniency as Mingxia had been.
translations.idiomatic: In deliberating on the offense of Regional Commander Ren Zhen he held a different opinion together with Mingxia and Jin Zhijun; he was convicted but shown leniency as Mingxia had been.

sentences.zh: 十二年，奏請依律定滿臣有罪籍沒家產、降革世職之例，下所司議行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized asking that the law be followed in fixing precedents for Manchu ministers guilty of offenses—confiscation of property and reduction or removal of hereditary offices—and the matter was sent down to the appropriate office for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he memorialized asking that the law be followed in fixing precedents for Manchu ministers guilty of offenses—confiscation of property and reduction or removal of hereditary offices—and the matter was referred to the appropriate office for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 復授弘文院大學士，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute and given the added titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute and given the added titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上幸南苑，召諸大臣入對，諭之遴曰：「朕不念爾前罪，屢申誥誡，嘗以朕言告人乎？

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor visited the Southern Park and summoned the great ministers for audience; he instructed Zhilin: "I do not hold your former offenses against you and have repeatedly issued admonitory edicts—have you ever told others what I have said?
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor visited the Southern Park and summoned the great ministers for audience; he instructed Zhilin: "I do not hold your former offenses against you and have repeatedly issued admonitory edicts—have you ever told others what I have said?

sentences.zh: 抑自思所行亦曾少改乎？」

translations.literal: Or do you yourself think your conduct has changed even a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Or do you yourself think your conduct has changed even a little?"

sentences.zh: 之遴奏曰：「上教臣，臣安敢不改？

translations.literal: Zhilin memorialized: "Your Majesty has instructed me—how would I dare not reform?
translations.idiomatic: Zhilin replied: "Your Majesty has instructed me—how would I dare not reform?

sentences.zh: 特臣才疏學淺，不能仰報上恩。」

translations.literal: It is only that my talent is meager and my learning shallow, and I cannot repay Your Majesty's grace from below."
translations.idiomatic: It is only that my talent is meager and my learning shallow, and I cannot repay Your Majesty's grace."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕非不知之遴等朋黨而用之，但欲資其才，故任以職。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is not that I do not know Zhilin and others form factions—I employ them only to make use of their talent, and therefore assign them office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "It is not that I do not know Zhilin and others form factions—I employ them only to make use of their talent, and therefore assign them office.

sentences.zh: 且時時教飭之者，亦冀其改過效忠耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover, in constantly instructing and admonishing them, I also hope they will reform their faults and serve loyally."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in constantly instructing and admonishing them, I also hope they will reform their faults and serve loyally."

sentences.zh: 因責左副都御史魏裔介等媕阿緘默，裔介退，具疏劾之遴植黨營私，當上詰問，但云「才疏學淺」，良心已昧；

translations.literal: He thereupon rebuked Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and others for fawning compliance and silence; Yijie withdrew and submitted a detailed memorial impeaching Zhilin for forming factions and pursuing private ends; when the emperor questioned him, he could only say "my talent is meager and my learning shallow"—his conscience was already clouded;
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon rebuked Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and others for fawning compliance and silence; Yijie withdrew and submitted a detailed memorial impeaching Zhilin for forming factions and pursuing private ends; when the emperor questioned him, he could only say "my talent is meager and my learning shallow"—his conscience was already clouded;

sentences.zh: 並言之遴諷禮部尚書胡世安舉知府沈令式，旋為總督李輝祖所劾，是為結黨之據。

translations.literal: he also stated that Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon memorialized against by Governor Li Huizu—this was evidence of faction forming.
translations.idiomatic: he also stated that Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon memorialized against by Governor-General Li Huizu—this was evidence of faction forming.

sentences.zh: 給事中王楨又劾之遴市權豪縱，昨蒙詰責，不思閉門省罪，即於次日遨遊靈佑宮，逍遙恣肆，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Zhen again memorialized against Zhilin for trading in power and acting with arrogant license; having just received imperial rebuke, he did not think to shut his doors and reflect on his guilt but on the very next day wandered at leisure in the Lingyou Palace, roaming freely and unrestrained—an offense that could not be spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Zhen again memorialized against Zhilin for trading in power and acting with arrogant license; having just received imperial rebuke, he did not think to shut his doors and reflect on his guilt but on the very next day wandered at leisure in the Lingyou Palace, roaming freely and unrestrained—an offense that could not be spared execution.

sentences.zh: 之遴疏引罪，有云：「南北各親其親，各友其友。」

translations.literal: Zhilin memorialized accepting guilt, stating: "North and south each honor their own kin and each befriend their own friends."
translations.idiomatic: Zhilin memorialized accepting guilt, stating: "North and south each honor their own kin and each befriend their own friends."

sentences.zh: 上益不懌，下吏部嚴議，命以原官發盛京居住。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more displeased; the matter was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel for strict deliberation, and he was ordered sent to live at Mukden under his former title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more displeased; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Personnel for strict deliberation, and he was ordered sent to live at Mukden under his former title.

sentences.zh: 是冬，復命回京入旗。

translations.literal: That winter he was again ordered to return to the capital and enter the banner.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was again ordered to return to the capital and enter the banner.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復坐賄結內監吳良輔，鞫實，論斬，命奪官，籍其家，流徙尚陽堡，死徙所。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was again convicted of bribing and forming ties with eunuch Wu Liangfu; when interrogation established the facts he was sentenced to decapitation; he was ordered stripped of office, his household property registered and confiscated, and he was exiled to Shangyang Fort, where he died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was again convicted of bribing and forming ties with eunuch Wu Liangfu; when interrogation established the facts he was sentenced to decapitation; he was stripped of office, his household property was confiscated, and he was exiled to Shangyang Fort, where he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 劉正宗，字可宗，山東安丘人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengzong, styled Kezong, was a native of Anqiu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengzong, styled Kezong, was a native of Anqiu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，自推官授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he was promoted from magistrate's aide to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Ming Chongzhen reign, he was promoted from magistrate's aide to compiler.

sentences.zh: 福王時，授中允。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he was appointed junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was appointed junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，以薦起國史院編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, on recommendation, he was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2, on recommendation, he was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to academician of the Secretariat Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to academician of the Secretariat Institute.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授吏部侍郎，擢弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書缺員，諭以「正宗清正耿介，堪勝此任，加太子太保，管吏部尚書」。

translations.literal: When the post of Minister of Personnel fell vacant, an edict stated: "Zhengzong is upright, pure, and firm—he can bear this responsibility; give him the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and charge him with managing the Ministry of Personnel."
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Minister of Personnel fell vacant, an edict stated: "Zhengzong is upright, pure, and firm—he can bear this responsibility; give him the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and charge him with managing the Ministry of Personnel."

sentences.zh: 御史楊義論部推越次，正宗與辨，執相詬詈。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Yi discussed ministry recommendations that skipped proper order; Zhengzong argued with him and they clung to each other in mutual abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Yi discussed ministry recommendations that skipped proper order; Zhengzong argued with him and they stubbornly exchanged mutual abuse.

sentences.zh: 給事中周曾發，御史姜圖南、祖建明交章劾之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhou Zengfa and censors Jiang Tunan and Zu Jianming jointly memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhou Zengfa and censors Jiang Tunan and Zu Jianming submitted joint memorials against him.

sentences.zh: 御史張嘉復以正宗昏庸衰老，背公徇私，疏請罷斥。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Jiafu, on the grounds that Zhengzong was muddled, aged, and pursued private ends against the public good, memorialized asking that he be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Jiafu memorialized asking that Zhengzong be dismissed on the grounds that he was muddled and aged and pursued private ends against the public good.

sentences.zh: 下部議，以無實據，寢其事。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the ministry for deliberation; because there was no substantiating evidence, the case was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation; because there was no substantiating evidence, the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 給事中硃徽复劾正宗擅擬僉事許宸遷通政司參議，不由會推，又未專疏題明。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhu Hui again memorialized against Zhengzong for on his own authority drafting the transfer of Vice Commissioner Xu Chen to Assistant Director of the Transmission Office, without joint recommendation and without a separate memorial stating it clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhu Hui again memorialized against Zhengzong for on his own authority drafting the transfer of Vice Commissioner Xu Chen to Assistant Director of the Transmission Office, without joint recommendation and without a separate memorial stating it clearly.

sentences.zh: 正宗以疏忽引咎，當俸，援恩詔以免。

translations.literal: Zhengzong accepted blame for negligence, was liable to salary reduction, and was exempted by citing the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzong accepted blame for negligence, was liable to salary reduction, and was exempted by citing the amnesty edict.

sentences.zh: 旋引疾乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he cited illness and asked to retire; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he cited illness and asked to retire; the request was not granted.

sentences.zh: 辭尚書，命以兼銜回內院，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He resigned the ministership and was ordered to return to the Inner Court with his concurrent title, given the added titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned the ministership and was ordered to return to the Inner Court under his concurrent title, with the added titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十四年，考滿，進少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when his assessment term was complete, he was promoted to Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when his assessment term was complete, he was promoted to Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was changed to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上以正宗器量狹隘，終日務詩文，廷議輒以己意為是，降旨嚴飭，並諭曰：「朕委任大臣，期始終相成，以愜簡拔初念。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because the emperor considered Zhengzong narrow in capacity, devoted all day to poetry and prose, and in court deliberations always held his own opinion correct, a stern admonitory edict was issued, also instructing: "I entrust great ministers expecting mutual completion from start to finish, to satisfy the original intent of selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, because the emperor considered Zhengzong narrow in capacity, devoted all day to poetry and prose, and in court deliberations always held his own opinion correct, a stern admonitory edict was issued, also instructing: "I entrust great ministers expecting mutual completion from start to finish, to satisfy the original intent of selection.

sentences.zh: 故不忍加罪，時加申戒。

translations.literal: Therefore I have been unwilling to punish him and have repeatedly issued warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have been unwilling to punish him and have repeatedly issued warnings.

sentences.zh: 當痛改前非，稱朕優容寬恕之意。」

translations.literal: He ought to reform his past faults thoroughly and respond to my intent of forbearance and forgiveness."
translations.idiomatic: He ought to reform his past faults thoroughly and respond to my intent of forbearance and forgiveness."

sentences.zh: 十七年，自陳乞罷，不允。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he memorialized on his own asking to be dismissed; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he memorialized on his own asking to be dismissed; the request was not granted.

sentences.zh: 左都御史魏裔介劾「正宗自陳奏內不敘上諭切責，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief of the Left Wei Yijie memorialized: "In his self-statement memorial Zhengzong did not recount the emperor's stern rebuke—this lacks the propriety of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief of the Left Wei Yijie memorialized: "In his self-statement memorial Zhengzong did not recount the emperor's stern rebuke—this lacks the propriety of a minister.

sentences.zh: 李昌祚叛案有名，票擬內升。

translations.literal: Li Changzuo was named in the rebel case, yet on the approval slip he was drafted for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changzuo was named in the rebel case, yet on the approval slip he was drafted for promotion.

sentences.zh: 先後薦董國祥、梁羽明，今皆事敗，被劾不自檢舉。

translations.literal: He had successively recommended Dong Guoxiang and Liang Yuming; now both their affairs have failed, yet when memorialized against he did not report himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had successively recommended Dong Guoxiang and Liang Yuming; now both their affairs have failed, yet when memorialized against he did not report himself.

sentences.zh: 欺君之罪何辭？

translations.literal: What excuse is there for the offense of deceiving the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: What excuse is there for the offense of deceiving the ruler?

sentences.zh: 正宗與張縉彥為友，縉彥序正宗詩曰'將明之才'，詭譎尤不可解。

translations.literal: Zhengzong and Zhang Jinyan were friends; Jinyan prefaced Zhengzong's poetry with the words "talent to govern and clarify," which is especially inexplicable and sinister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzong and Zhang Jinyan were friends; Jinyan prefaced Zhengzong's poetry with the words "talent to govern and clarify," which is especially inexplicable and sinister.

sentences.zh: 正宗弟正學，為鄭成功總兵，正宗囑巡撫耿焞躐升中軍。

translations.literal: Zhengzong's younger brother Zhengxue was a regional commander under Zheng Chenggong; Zhengzong instructed Governor Geng Tun to promote him by skipping ranks to middle army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzong's younger brother Zhengxue was a regional commander under Zheng Chenggong; Zhengzong instructed Governor Geng Tun to promote him by skipping ranks to middle army commander.
